ROLE: Perform one nonblocking send with MSG_NOSIGNAL, retrying EINTR internally and reporting progress, would-block or a fatal error with the exact number of bytes accepted.

SIGNATURE.RAW: enum net_io_result net_write_some(int fd, const uint8_t *buf, size_t len, size_t *out_n)
SIGNATURE.NAME: net_write_some

FUNC.NAME: send
FUNC.ROLE: one nonblocking write of at most len bytes from the caller's queue

VAR.NAME: MSG_NOSIGNAL
VAR.ROLE: suppress SIGPIPE on a peer that closed, so a dead peer cannot kill the broker

VAR.NAME: EINTR
VAR.ROLE: retry the send after a signal

CALL_CONTRACTS.NAME: send
CALL_CONTRACTS.SIGNATURE: ssize_t send(int fd, const void *buf, size_t len, int flags)
CALL_CONTRACTS.RETURN: the number of bytes accepted (1..len), or -1 with errno set (EINTR, EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK, EPIPE/ECONNRESET)
CALL_CONTRACTS.OWNERSHIP: buf is only read; the caller keeps the bytes until *out_n of them are reported written
CALL_CONTRACTS.FAILURE: -1 is classified by errno: EINTR retries, EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK becomes NET_IO_WOULD_BLOCK, anything else becomes NET_IO_ERROR and the caller closes the session after releasing its queue

LOGIC.INPUT: fd: a nonblocking peer descriptor (mode set by net_accept). buf/len: the bytes to write, normally the leading unflushed bytes of the session output buffer, so the caller consumes exactly the reported count afterwards. out_n: bytes accepted by the kernel.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If out_n is NULL return NET_IO_ERROR; *out_n = 0. 2) If fd < 0 or buf is NULL return NET_IO_ERROR. 3) If len == 0 { *out_n = 0; return NET_IO_WOULD_BLOCK; } - a zero-length write is a documented no-op reported as no progress so that a drain loop that only continues on NET_IO_PROGRESS cannot spin; the caller never passes an empty buffer because it checks the queue first. 4) Loop: n = send(fd, buf, len, MSG_NOSIGNAL); if n > 0 { *out_n = (size_t)n; return NET_IO_PROGRESS; } if n == 0 return NET_IO_ERROR (a zero-length acceptance for a nonzero request is not progress and must not be reported as such); if n < 0: if errno == EINTR continue; if errno == EAGAIN || errno == EWOULDBLOCK return NET_IO_WOULD_BLOCK; else return NET_IO_ERROR. 5) Because the descriptor is nonblocking and only one send is attempted per call, a peer with a full socket buffer never blocks the loop; the caller stops and waits for EPOLLOUT. MSG_NOSIGNAL means a peer that vanished produces EPIPE/ECONNRESET instead of a fatal SIGPIPE (SIGPIPE is also ignored in main as a second line of defence). The remaining bytes stay in the caller's buffer, so a partial write is always resumable: the caller consumes exactly *out_n and keeps the rest.
LOGIC.OUTPUT: NET_IO_PROGRESS with *out_n in 1..len when some bytes were accepted: the caller must consume exactly *out_n bytes from the front of its queue and keep sending later. NET_IO_WOULD_BLOCK with *out_n == 0 when the socket buffer is full or len was 0. NET_IO_ERROR with *out_n == 0 for NULL/invalid arguments, a zero-length acceptance or a fatal write error.
INVARIANTS_USED: the descriptor is nonblocking so a single send is bounded and cannot stall unrelated peers
partial writes are legal and the unaccepted bytes must stay queued
MSG_NOSIGNAL prevents a per-peer write failure from terminating the process
the caller consumes exactly the bytes the kernel accepted, so no byte is written twice
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: fd is NULL or a valid nonblocking descriptor; buf points to len readable bytes when len > 0.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: On progress the first *out_n bytes of buf were accepted by the kernel and the buffer is otherwise untouched; on any other result no byte was accepted.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Safe per descriptor; concurrent writes on the same descriptor could reorder bytes.
